A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DSO study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, references and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across the appendix expansion and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original TRELLIS fine-tuning experiments, physical simulations, baseline comparisons, scaling studies and evaluations on real-world images.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds simulator-transfer, perturbation, mesh-cutting and DRO training-length evaluations.

M1.justification: DSO still labels generated assets using simulation feedback and fine-tunes TRELLIS's first transformer using LoRA and the same DRO or DPO objectives. The new appendix material analyzes and evaluates this existing procedure.

E1.justification: The Objaverse-based datasets, synthetic-image training and real-world alarm-clock/motorcycle evaluations are retained. Appendix D.1 adds distinct evaluation environments: Isaac Gym and randomly tilted initial poses in MuJoCo, without adding object categories or datasets.

E2.justification: Appendix D.2 and Table 7 add a post-processing comparator that cuts meshes flat, evaluated at four heights. Existing TRELLIS, Atlas3D, PhysComp and supervised fine-tuning comparisons remain; Table 6 extends the existing comparator sets to additional simulation conditions.

E3.justification: Existing training settings and the 65-object and 11-object evaluations are unchanged. Added experiments introduce Isaac Gym evaluation, initial-rotation bounds of 0.01, 0.02, 0.04 and 0.08, four mesh-cutting heights, and DRO checkpoints from 2,000 to 5,000 training steps.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands robustness and sensitivity analysis. Table 6 tests transfer beyond the training simulator and sensitivity to initial rotations; Appendix E and Table 8 extend the training-compute analysis from DPO to DRO, documenting deterioration after extended training.

E5.justification: Appendix D.1 newly reports averaging stability over 100 simulation runs per perturbation bound. This describes repetition for the added randomized evaluation, without establishing additional training seeds or introducing confidence intervals for retained results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and 5 retain their results, while Tables 6–8 substantially expand the empirical findings. On the full evaluation set, new DRO results include 93.7% stability under the largest perturbation versus TRELLIS's 77.2%, and 99.6% in Isaac Gym versus 97.3%. New mesh-cutting comparisons and DRO checkpoints also document geometric tradeoffs, including Chamfer distance worsening from 0.0440 at 4,000 steps to 0.0853 at 5,000 steps.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds a limited mathematical analysis of loss monotonicity and derivatives, contrasting DRO's constant derivative with DPO's decaying derivative in Figure 8. The original objectives and Appendix A derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: simulation-feedback alignment, DRO without pairwise preferences, training from generated data, and faster, more reliable stable-object generation. Revised wording and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new evaluations as evidence of simulator generalization and attributes DRO's faster convergence to its nonsaturating derivative relative to DPO. It also extends the overtraining warning to DRO. The existing limitation concerning scarce positive samples is retained, moving from Appendix E to F.

D1.justification: The added appendices specify random-angle initialization and mesh cutting above the lowest vertex, with concrete perturbation bounds and cutting heights. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, inference settings, timing and access information are retained.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 116 works and retain the same positioning relative to physics-based test-time optimization and generative-model alignment. The added experiments reuse existing Atlas3D and Isaac Gym references.

P1.justification: v2 makes sentence-level copyedits throughout the abstract and main text while preserving the narrative and main section sequence. Appendix D gains subsections, a new discussion appendix E is inserted, and the former limitations appendix becomes F.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6–8 and the two-panel loss/derivative Figure 8. Existing displays are preserved, with Figure 7 relocated and surrounding material reflowed; there is no broad redesign of the original figures or tables.

improvement.justification: The added simulator-transfer and perturbation tests strengthen physical-robustness evidence, while the cutting baseline and DRO scaling study clarify alternatives and training tradeoffs. These are useful incremental gains for the unchanged method. Superiority across conditions requires qualification for DPO: Table 6 reports 67.5% stability versus PhysComp's 67.7% on the 11-object subset at the largest perturbation, although DRO remains ahead.
